reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Hypersegmented neutrophils are the earliest blood sign of megaloblastic change
Only B12 deficiency causes subacute combined degeneration
Folate stores last months; B12 stores last years
Check B12 before folate therapy to avoid masking cord injury
reference.pathophysiology: B12 and folate enable thymidine synthesis for DNA replication. Their lack desynchronises nuclear and cytoplasmic maturation, causing megaloblasts, ineffective haematopoiesis and pancytopenia in severe cases. B12 additionally maintains myelin through methylation, explaining cord and brain injury unique to its deficiency.
additionalDifferentials: Pernicious anaemia versus dietary B12 deficiency
additionalInvestigations: Blood film for macroovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils
Serum B12 and folate with methylmalonic acid in borderline cases
Intrinsic factor antibody for pernicious anaemia
